interface.title: DepremNabız AI — Türkiye Seismic Intelligence & Resilience Platform
interface.field: Seismology / earthquake hazard and exposure analytics (with Sentinel-1 InSAR discovery)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis and screening of earthquake catalogues; decision-support prototyping
interface.what_it_is_for: Load a Türkiye earthquake catalogue (synthetic demo, live USGS, or an uploaded CSV/Excel file), read summary statistics and a Gutenberg-Richter b-value, look at maps, time series and distributions, screen for statistical event-rate anomalies, count nearby exposure points around each event, and browse Sentinel-1 acquisitions, candidate pairs and processed InSAR displacement points.

data.note: I started from the built-in synthetic demo catalogue (620 events, latest 2026-08-02) with its 180 synthetic exposure points and demo Sentinel-1 catalogue. I also used the uploaded test files earthquakes_upload.csv, exposure_points_upload.csv and displacement_points.csv. The server did have network access: Live USGS returned 6 records (30 days, M≥2.1) and then 19 records (90 days, M≥1.5), and Live Copernicus STAC returned real Sentinel-1C/1D GRD items.

tree.general: Characterise recent seismicity in a region, screen it for unusual activity and nearby assets, and line up satellite deformation data
tree.specific: Explore a Türkiye earthquake catalogue in DepremNabız AI: b-value, anomaly screen, DBSCAN clusters, urban exposure within a radius, and Sentinel-1/InSAR deformation

children.specific: Pick the sidebar Mode (Demo data / Live USGS / Upload local file) and read the source banner (source · record count · latest timestamp)

children.general: Change the completeness cutoff and see how the scaling estimate shifts
children.specific: Move the Minimum magnitude slider from 1.50 to 2.10. The slider filters events only in Live USGS mode (as a query parameter); in Demo and Upload modes it only sets the b-value cutoff, which never goes below 1.0. So in demo mode the event count stays at 620 (events of M 1.2 remain on the map) and only the b-value changes (0.64 → 0.66)

children.label: pressed PageUp on Minimum magnitude slider (1.50 → 2.10)

children.general: Review data-quality metrics of a clean reference table as a baseline
children.specific: Demo-mode baseline on the Data quality tab: rows 620, valid_time_share 1, valid_coordinate_share 1, magnitude_completeness 1, duplicate_event_ids 0, invalid_coordinates 0. Compare against the uploaded catalogue in the import task (screens/042.webp)

children.general: Pull live records from an authoritative public catalogue with a time window and magnitude threshold
children.specific: Live USGS mode: banner reads 'Official USGS Earthquake Catalog API'. 30 days and M≥2.1 gave 6 records (max 5.1); 90 days and M≥1.5 gave 19 records (max 5.2); b-value shows n/a. The replay confirmed only the 30-day case

pressed PageDown on Minimum magnitude slider (2.10 → 1.50)

children.general: Import your own messy table and check how it was cleaned
children.specific: Upload local file: earthquakes_upload.csv → 'User-supplied local catalogue · records: 8', max 7.8. The aliased columns were mapped, and the exported CSV has 8 rows and lacks tr-upload-006. Confirmed defect: clean_events drops invalid-coordinate and duplicate-ID rows before quality_report runs (streamlit_app.py:64,79; pipeline.py:84-89), so the Data quality tab shows duplicate_event_ids 0 and invalid_coordinates 0 and the dropped rows are never reported

children.specific: Synthetic demo exposure (180 points). The screen covers the 50 largest-magnitude events (frame.nlargest(50, 'magnitude'), streamlit_app.py:192) and lists event_id, magnitude, nearby_points, exposure_weight and radius_km, sorted by exposure_weight, plus an Exposure points map coloured by category

At 50 km tr-upload-001 has 2 nearby points (weight 811444); at 115 km tr-upload-003 leads with 4 points (1130044); at 10 km only tr-upload-009 has 1 point. Missing weights count as 1.0 in the table (exposure.py:27), but they reach the map as NaN, so the Exposure points map does not render (see screens_never_reached)

children.general: Read how results may and may not be interpreted

children.general: Check interpretation rules and scope limits
children.specific: Anomaly = statistical deviation, not a forecast; b-value depends on completeness; clusters come from DBSCAN parameters (fixed in code, no UI control); exposure ≠ damage; deformation processing belongs in SNAP/ISCE/GMTSAR/MintPy

features.name: Switchable data-source loader with provenance banner
features.general: Choose between a bundled example, a live web feed (with time window and threshold) or an uploaded file; every view then recomputes, and a banner states source, record count and latest timestamp
features.specific: Sidebar Mode radio (Demo data / Live USGS / Upload local file) with Live lookback (days) and Minimum magnitude sliders and a CSV/XLSX uploader; green banner 'Source: … · records: N · latest: …' and five metric cards (Events, Maximum magnitude, Median depth, Shallow share ≤20 km, b-value)
steps: Pick a mode in the sidebar radio
For live mode, set lookback days and minimum magnitude
For upload mode, drop a CSV/Excel file
Read the source banner and the metric cards
serves_tasks: Open the bundled example dataset and read headline statistics
Pull live records from an authoritative public catalogue with a time window and magnitude threshold
Import your own messy table and check how it was cleaned

features.name: Cutoff-dependent scaling estimate
features.general: Recompute a power-law magnitude–frequency slope when a completeness cutoff is changed, without removing events below the cutoff from the other views
features.specific: b-value estimate card driven by the Minimum magnitude slider (floor 1.0). Moving the slider 1.50 → 2.10 changes the b-value 0.64 → 0.66 while Events stays 620; it filters events only in Live USGS mode. Shows n/a for small catalogues
serves_tasks: Change the completeness cutoff and see how the scaling estimate shifts

features.name: Rolling-baseline anomaly screen chart
features.general: Plot a daily count series against its rolling baseline and mark days that exceed it; inspect flagged points by hover, hide series via the legend, and box-zoom into a window
features.specific: Rolling event-rate anomaly screen (Daily count, 14-day Rolling baseline, red-X Screened anomaly at |z|≥2.5; settings fixed in code) with Plotly hover, legend toggle, zoom box and double-click reset
steps: Hover a red X to read its date and count
Click a legend entry to hide the raw count
Drag a box to zoom into the period
serves_tasks: Flag days with unusually high event rates against a rolling baseline (statistical, not a forecast)

features.name: Event map with cluster labels on hover
features.general: Show point events on a pannable, zoomable basemap, coloured and sized by a value, with a hover card giving each point's attributes and its spatial-cluster label
features.specific: Earthquake-event map (Plotly scattermap on OpenStreetMap) coloured by magnitude; hover shows place, lat/lon, time_utc, depth_km, source, DBSCAN cluster (eps 35 km, min_samples 4, fixed), magnitude. It opens at 0°,0° and must be panned to Türkiye
steps: Scroll the wheel to zoom out
Drag to pan to the study region
Hover a marker to read its attributes and cluster id
serves_tasks: Locate events on a map and inspect each event's spatial-cluster label

features.name: Radius-based proximity screening of assets around events
features.general: Upload a list of asset locations (with optional weights and categories), set a search radius, and get per-event counts and summed weights of assets within that distance for the largest events, plus a category map
features.specific: Urban exposure tab: Exposure points CSV uploader, Screening radius (km) slider (5–150), table of event_id / magnitude / nearby_points / exposure_weight / radius_km for the 50 largest-magnitude events, sorted by weight (missing weights count as 1.0), Exposure points map by category; falls back to 180 synthetic points
steps: Upload an exposure-points CSV, or keep the synthetic demo points
Read the per-event nearby_points and exposure_weight
Pan the Exposure points map to the region
serves_tasks: Count assets within a set distance of each event using the built-in points
Upload your own asset list and repeat the screen at different radii

features.name: Satellite acquisition search with repeat-pass pair builder
features.general: Search an imagery archive (demo or live) for a date range, list the scenes, and derive candidate same-track image pairs with their time gaps
features.specific: Satellite catalogue radio (Demo catalogue / Live Copernicus STAC), Start/End date pickers, Search Sentinel-1 acquisitions button, acquisitions table and Candidate same-orbit pairs table (reference_id, secondary_id, gap_days, relative_orbit, orbit_state)
steps: Choose Demo catalogue or Live Copernicus STAC

features.name: Point-measurement upload with summary statistics and value-coloured map

features.specific: Optional processed InSAR points CSV (latitude, longitude, displacement_mm) → JSON summary (points, median_mm, min_mm, max_mm, p95_abs_mm) and 'Uploaded displacement points' map with a diverging displacement_mm colour scale
